Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Dr. S.B.Maurya, learned AGA-I, for the State, apprised the Court that on 12.8.2023 notice has been served to the informant of the case.
2. Despite service of notice, none appeared on behalf of the informant.

3. Heard Sri Amit Kumar, learned counsel for the applicant and Dr.S.B.Maurya, learned AGA-I, for the State.
4.

The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No.100 of 2023, under Sections 328 and 376 IPC, Section 3/4 POCSO Act and Section 67 Information Technology Act, Police Station Bilari, District Moradabad during pendency of the trial.

5. FIR of the present case was lodged on 18.3.2023, under Sections 328 and 376 IPC against the applicant and according to the FIR, about two years before applicant after administering some Kailash vs State Of U.P. sentences.text: intoxicating substances made physical relationship with the daughter of the informant and also prepared her obscene photographs and when daughter of the informant stopped to make conversation with him then he viraled her photographs.

6. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that entire allegation made against the applicant is totally false and baseless and from the perusal of the FIR it appears that on the basis of stale allegation of two years old, applicant has been made accused in the present matter.

7. He further submits that even as per statements of the victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. in May, 2022 applicant made physical relationship with her and also prepared her obscene photographs and all the allegations prima facie appear to be false as for almost a year prosecutrix kept herself mum.
8. He further submits that there is no evidence on record except the bald allegation that applicant either prepared the obscene photographs of the victim or viraled the same.

9. He further submits that from the perusal of the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. it appears that the alleged photograph which was alleged to have been sent by applicant was of applicant and victim and in that photograph both were kissing, therefore, it cannot be said that this photograph was obscene one.

10. He further submits that applicant is not having any previous criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 5.4.2023, i.e., for five months.
11.
Per contra, learned AGA although opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that FIR of the present case was lodged after about a year from the date of alleged rape.
12. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

13. Considering the fact that FIR of the present case was lodged after almost a year from the date of alleged rape and from the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Sections 164 Cr.P.C. it appears that the alleged photograph of the victim and the applicant was not of obscene one, in my view, applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
14. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

15. Let the applicant-Kailash be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

sentences.text: (ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
16. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

17. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
